goal: Allow flow get resolve-context to accept the standard flow target guards and route them through existing target validation while preserving guard-free behavior.

analysis.problem: The get.resolve-context registry definition exposes neither dispatcher options nor help for --expect-run-id, --expect-issue, and --expect-spec, so guarded calls fail as unknown options before the shared flow target validation can run.
analysis.proposedApproach: Register the existing FLOW_TARGET_GUARD_OPTIONS constant on get.resolve-context, describe the same options in its help text, and rely on FlowCommand plus flow-context for selection and ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH behavior.
analysis.validation: Verify registry/help parity, successful dispatch with matching run ID, Issue, and spec guards, ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH for each mismatching guard, and unchanged success without guards.

knownFacts: The registry already defines FLOW_TARGET_GUARD_OPTIONS as --expect-issue, --expect-spec, and --expect-run-id.
FlowCommand already calls shared flow-context resolution and targetMismatchEnvelopeForInput before command execution.
The existing resolve-context registry entry has no args.options and its help contains no target guard options.
Existing extended tests cover guard-free resolve-context behavior and resolved data fields.
The refined Issue and flow assignment confirm one bounded registry-and-tests bug fix with shared validation reuse and no finalize-commit change.
resolvedByProjectRules: must: Reuse FLOW_TARGET_GUARD_OPTIONS and the existing FlowCommand/flow-context validation path instead of duplicating validation.
must: Keep the change within src/flow/registry.js and the two named unit-test files, apart from Senti-generated artifacts.
must: Add no external dependency and preserve calls that omit all target guards.
deferredToSpec: must: Define requirement identifiers, task decomposition, and concrete test scenarios for help parity and target guard dispatch.

in: must: Add FLOW_TARGET_GUARD_OPTIONS to the get.resolve-context registry definition.
must: Display --expect-run-id, --expect-issue, and --expect-spec in resolve-context help with dispatcher parity.
must: Test matching guards, each individual mismatch as ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH, and existing guard-free success.
out: must: Do not change finalize-commit, implement Issues #410 through #428, add duplicate validation or guard bypasses, or add dependencies.
must: Do not modify files outside the three Issue targets except Senti-required spec, evidence, and generated documentation artifacts.

impactOnExisting: must: Guarded resolve-context calls that currently fail option parsing must reach existing shared target validation.
must: Matching guards must return the same resolved context payload as unguarded calls.
must: Calls without guards must continue to succeed without behavior changes.
must: Mismatched run ID, Issue, or spec must use the established ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH envelope.

qa.question: must: Should Issue #429 be implemented exactly as the bounded registry-and-tests bug fix described here, including shared validation reuse, guard-free compatibility, and the stated exclusions?
qa.answer: must: Yes. Implement the refined Issue exactly within the three named product/test files, reusing the standard target guard machinery and preserving guard-free calls.

qa.why: The registry metadata gap is the root cause, while FlowCommand and flow-context already own matching and ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH behavior.
